special_attention.run_capture_vs_not_in_a_capture: Nothing on the list is written. Fork stage files = ordinary stage records of each fork (masked slot transcripts, M / A / H openings with published salts); the tail = S1 and the B_k / endpoint openings as write_pcs writes a D12a IO opening; run.json = write_run's header words, layout, D55 text and the SAME not_in_a_capture list (run_capture.rs:3288); arrays.bin = merged per-fork stores (absorb_store copies only stored arrays, :792-836); receipt/ = the receipt's own frames. ALLOWED_KEYS (:4035-4360) has no hunk r19b -> HEAD, and every key the fork writers emit (tail: schema, kind, blocks, end_tag, opening_order, header, state, next, roles, transcript_sites, stage, site, before, after) is on it. The recorder is attached only on the verifier (run_fork.rs capture calls :1279-1476), seeded from public words (ForkSeed :1157).
special_attention.fork_randomness: L + 1 generators per run, each ZkRng::from_os under its own domain: the commit phase's (run_fork.rs:1095, used only by boundary::prepare for the L-1 boundaries :1104, dropped :1107 before any fork) and one per fork inside its worker (:1022, handed to prove_core by &mut). from_os reads 32 fresh bytes of /dev/urandom per call and keys BLAKE3 with them (zkp-core rng.rs:44-65; digest f6728bd2, read in W16_READINGS); the domains (SEED_USE ‖ ROLE_RUN_PROVER ‖ k ‖ profile, :371-384) only add separation. ZkRng is not Clone (rng.rs:9-14); the file has no ZkRng::new; a production Cheat is the honest constants. Independence therefore rests on independent OS draws, as D12a's one run generator rests on one.
special_attention.d55_join: absorb_join (run_fork.rs:864-871) absorbs k, the fork transcript's 32-byte state ‖ squeeze counter, and the slot-21 / slot-22 claim lists (claim_bytes :843-860: count, value, part count, slice offset, log size, coefficient, point). The verifier absorbs its OWN values (verify_one_fork :1284-1290 returns verify_core's [ic, oc] and its own end state; join :1391-1394), so the transcript only matches if the prover's words equal what the verifier recomputes from the receipt; the claims are the D12a IO claims (masked by their reserved pairs, PG-8), are not written into any fork frame (ForkFrame :47-55), and are opened only in the tail. Verifier-computable words only.
special_attention.f3_marker: D55_REAL_CONTENT_PRIVACY_GATE_PASSED = false (run_fork.rs:101). stack-prove --d55-workers is refused before anything is read unless --d55-test-receipt-not-for-publication is given (trained_block.rs d55_prove_admission :2690-2703, call :3053); the marker is a fixed text, create_new + flush + rename, never replaced (:1541-1555), admitted by the reader only as exactly that text (:1524-1536, :1646-1650), absorbed nowhere, in no frame, not in segments.json or statement.json; stack-verify reports it and prints not_for_publication = marked || !gate (:3409-3427). Operational, not cryptographic (N-R26-R3).
special_attention.reader_error_messages: Every new or changed reader error carries a path, a directory entry name, a byte length, an index k or L, or an OS error string: read_segment_bounded / read_regular_file_bounded (run.rs:1715, :1752, text unchanged), read_frame_bounded / read_fork_receipt / the marker (run_fork.rs:1590-1683, :1524-1536), decode_* (run_fork_wire.rs), token tables (load.rs:130), tied tables (tied_tables.rs:30), the batch request (classify_batch.rs:119-124, OS error only, content never echoed). The verifier holds no witness. notes.what: The D60 privacy-gate records' bundles pin the dd81ab4f digests of five of these files (run.rs 604b65b1, run_capture.rs 5d5fdfcc, trained_block.rs 4d1e24bd, run_fork.rs e7b58ff7, run_fork_wire.rs a2dbc6f1); load.rs and tied_tables.rs are at r19b there, classify_batch.rs is unpinned. This file reads both the HEAD digests and (chained, dd81ab4f -> HEAD = commit ed519548's F3 / F4 / F7 / F8 and description-text hunks only) the dd81ab4f digests, so the coordinator can wire either. A bundle written at HEAD carries the HEAD digests.

The capture's join replay (`fork_join`, run_capture.rs:1338) takes the claim lists from the verifier rather than re-deriving them; they are public words the verifier computed, so this is a capture-independence point, not a leak. The Python gate's D55-IO part derives the joined claims from each fork's slot-21 / slot-22 terminals independently (privacy_gate/README.md section 2).

The F3 marker is operational, not cryptographic: `--d55-test-receipt-not-for-publication` admits any content, and the marker is not bound to the frames (removing it leaves a receipt that verifies). While the constant is false, `stack-verify` prints `not_for_publication: true` for every D55 receipt, marked or not (trained_block.rs:3409-3427). D60's text already says so.

Prover stdout now carries per-fork `prove_core` seconds (`d55-proved`) and, under HL_PB_TIMING, per-phase durations and GPU byte counts (classify_run.rs, classify_cli.rs). Prover-private under P-6, the same class as D12a's per-segment `elapsed_seconds`; nothing enters a receipt, statement or capture. An app that relays prover stdout should keep treating it as private.

D60 F4 lifts the macOS run-time refusal of `prove-batch`'s request reader (classify_batch.rs:48, :119). prove-batch remains outside D58's accepted scope and R18-1 (the app's batch quarantine) is still open (round 24 section 6.5).

`classify_cli::door` (not a capture pin) differs r19b -> HEAD by three HL_PB_TIMING lines; a tool that compares the door text against r17 / r19b (round 24's `classify_cli_door_r17_equals_r19b`) would report a difference that is diagnostic only.

`write_fork_receipt` creates each `.partial` with `File::create` after an emptiness check (run_fork.rs:1575), the same pattern as `run_sink::DirSink` (run_sink.rs:195); a symlink raced into the prover's own run directory would be followed. Receipt bytes are public, so this is write-path hygiene, not privacy.
